raw.Connection Title: Pemphigus vulgaris clinical and biopsy clues
raw.Explanation: Pemphigus vulgaris combines fragile intraepidermal blisters and frequent mucosal disease with keratinocyte separation and a net-like intercellular IgG pattern.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Pemphigus vulgaris; Autoimmune desmosomal blistering
raw.Source Section: Autoimmune Blistering Conditions > Pemphigus Vulgaris and Summary, PDF pp. 73, 76
raw.Notes: Verified: suprabasal acantholysis, fishnet/intercellular IgG on DIF, anti-desmoglein 3 +/- 1. Added refs: Schmidt E et al, Lancet 2019; Kasperkiewicz M et al, Nat Rev Dis Primers 2017.

raw.Explanation: DRESS refers to a delayed drug reaction with an exanthem, eosinophilia, and systemic manifestations. The group describes a characteristic syndrome rather than mandatory findings at every time point.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms; DRESS features
raw.Source Section: Reactive Disease > DRESS Syndrome, PDF p. 80
raw.Notes: Verified: latency 2-8 weeks, morbilliform eruption (near-universal), eosinophilia (~52-95%, time-variable), multiorgan involvement (liver most common). raw.Explanation: The source presents allergic contact dermatitis as a delayed, T-cell-mediated response involving antigen presentation, inflammatory signaling, and intercellular epidermal edema.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Type IV contact hypersensitivity; Allergic contact dermatitis pathway
raw.Source Section: Atopic and Allergic Disease > Allergic Contact Dermatitis, PDF p. 83
raw.Notes: Verified type IV (delayed) hypersensitivity pathway plus its histologic consequence (spongiosis). Added refs: Kabashima K et al, Nat Rev Immunol 2019; Tong Y et al, Front Immunol 2026.

raw.Explanation: The source identifies these settings as associated with cutaneous SCC. Chronic wounds and burn scars represent persistent local injury contexts; exposure and immune status provide additional risk pathways.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Cutaneous SCC risk factors; Squamous cell skin cancer risk settings
raw.Source Section: Skin Cancer > Squamous Cell Carcinoma and Summary, PDF pp. 96, 99
raw.Notes: Independently verified, including burn scars (Marjolin ulcer: ~92-94% SCC, ~30-year latency). Arsenic is an IARC Group 1 carcinogen; organ-transplant/immunosuppression markedly raises risk. Impaired-wound-healing overlaps the first two tiles but not all four. Added refs: Wysong A, N Engl J Med 2023; Burusapat C et al, J Burn Care Res 2021; NCCN Squamous Cell Skin Cancer 2026.

raw.Explanation: Bacillary angiomatosis is linked to Bartonella and vascular skin lesions, with bacteria demonstrable by a silver stain and a neutrophil-rich inflammatory component.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Bacillary angiomatosis; Bartonella-associated vascular proliferation
raw.Source Section: Vascular Tumors > Bacillary Angiomatosis, PDF p. 112
raw.Notes: Verified (B. henselae/quintana; lobular vascular proliferation with neutrophils around bacterial aggregates; Warthin-Starry positive). Neutrophilic infiltrate is frequent but variable; Warthin-Starry is not specific/always positive. Clinically mimics pyogenic granuloma and Kaposi sarcoma. Added refs: Adal KA et al, N Engl J Med 1994; Cockerell CJ, LeBoit PE, J Am Acad Dermatol 1990.

raw.Explanation: Kaposi sarcoma is associated with HHV-8, purple lesions, and spindle-cell histology. HIV-associated immune dysfunction is an important risk context rather than a universal feature.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Kaposi sarcoma; HHV-8-associated vascular tumor
raw.Source Section: Vascular Tumors > Kaposi Sarcoma, PDF p. 113
raw.Notes: Verified: HHV-8/KSHV is etiologic in all forms; CD31/CD34/LANA-positive spindle cells; HIV elevates risk up to ~20,000-fold but KS also occurs in classic/endemic/iatrogenic forms. HHV-8 and HIV play distinct roles and are not interchangeable causes. Added refs: Cesarman E et al, Nat Rev Dis Primers 2019; Yarchoan R, Uldrick TS, N Engl J Med 2018; Li JJ et al, Am J Pathol 1996.

raw.Explanation: Acanthosis nigricans produces velvety hyperpigmented plaques, often in folds. It is commonly linked to insulin resistance, while an abrupt presentation can raise concern for a malignant association.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Acanthosis nigricans; Benign and malignant acanthosis nigricans associations
raw.Source Section: Benign Dark Skin Lesions > Acanthosis Nigricans, PDF p. 117
raw.Notes: Verified: insulin resistance (benign, common) and malignant AN (abrupt, ~60% gastric adenocarcinoma, TGF-alpha/EGFR driven) are distinct contexts, not features required together. Most cases are benign -- do not imply most signal cancer. Board-overlap warning: shares a paraneoplastic/gastric-cancer axis with DERM-038 (Leser-Trelat); the two frequently co-occur. Added refs: Valejo Coelho MM et al, JAMA Dermatol 2019; Gillespie J et al, Am J Clin Dermatol 2026.

raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Seborrheic keratosis; SK appearance and eruptive pattern
raw.Source Section: Benign Dark Skin Lesions > Seborrheic Keratosis, PDF p. 118
raw.Notes: Verified morphology and eruptive Leser-Trelat concept (classically gastric/GI adenocarcinoma). Caveat: the paraneoplastic validity of Leser-Trelat is debated (a large Swedish cohort found no cancer association), so present it as a classic sign, not proven/universal. Board-overlap warning: shares the paraneoplastic/gastric-cancer axis with DERM-037. Added refs: Schwartz RA, J Am Acad Dermatol 1996; Husain Z et al, J Drugs Dermatol 2013; Lindelof B et al, J Am Acad Dermatol 1992.

raw.Connection Title: Hypothalamic hormones that stimulate anterior pituitary secretion

raw.Source Section: Hypothalamus: Function, p. 7; Anterior Pituitary: Function, p. 16
raw.Notes: Verified stimulatory (releasing) hormones; dopamine and somatostatin are the inhibitory counterparts and are correct distractors. Ref: Molina PE, Endocrine Physiology 5e (McGraw Hill); Van Uytfanghe K et al., Thyroid 2023.

raw.Connection Title: Acquired causes of central diabetes insipidus
raw.Explanation: These processes can injure the hypothalamic-neurohypophyseal system and reduce effective ADH secretion, producing central diabetes insipidus.

raw.Source Section: Diabetes Insipidus: Pathophysiology, p. 10
raw.Notes: TBI, SAH, meningitis, and Langerhans cell histiocytosis are established acquired causes of central DI; not inevitable. Ref: Refardt J et al. Clin Endocrinol 2019; Driano JE et al. Pediatrics 2021 (DI vs SIADH).

raw.Connection Title: Dopamine-blocking drugs that can elevate prolactin
raw.Explanation: Dopamine normally suppresses lactotroph secretion. Blocking dopamine receptors can remove that inhibition and cause hyperprolactinemia.

raw.Source Section: Hyperprolactinemia: Pathophysiology, p. 20
raw.Notes: Risperidone, haloperidol, fluphenazine (antipsychotic D2 antagonists) and metoclopramide (prokinetic D2 antagonist) cause hyperprolactinemia by disinhibition; metoclopramide prevents an 'all-antipsychotic' reading. Ref: Katzung Basic & Clinical Pharmacology 15e.

raw.Connection Title: Drugs that reduce peripheral T4-to-T3 conversion
raw.Explanation: The source lists PTU, beta blockers, glucocorticoids and amiodarone as inhibitors of peripheral thyroid hormone conversion. Propranolol is the beta blocker named elsewhere in the thyroid section.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Peripheral deiodination inhibitors; Drugs inhibiting T4 activation
raw.Source Section: T3, T4 Synthesis and Pharmacology, p. 25; Graves Disease: Management, p. 26
raw.Notes: Confirmed inhibitors of peripheral T4-to-T3 (type I 5'-deiodinase): PTU, glucocorticoids, amiodarone, and propranolol. QUALIFIER: propranolol inhibits conversion only at high dose (>160 mg/day) and the effect is not clinically relevant at usual doses; do not generalize to all beta-blockers. Ref: Burch HB. Drug Effects on the Thyroid. NEJM 2019; Van Uytfanghe K et al. Thyroid 2023; FDA levothyroxine label.

raw.Connection Title: Components of the source thyroid-storm regimen
raw.Explanation: The source four-part regimen combines adrenergic control, a thionamide, a glucocorticoid and iodine. This is a regimen association, not a shared mechanism.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Four Ps of thyroid storm; Source-listed thyroid storm therapies
raw.Source Section: Graves Disease: Complications, p. 26
raw.Notes: ATA-supported thyroid-storm regimen: thionamide (PTU) + beta-blocker (propranolol) + glucocorticoid + iodide (KI). CRITICAL QUALIFIER: iodide must be given >=1 h AFTER the thionamide; not simultaneous or a universally required set. ATA names hydrocortisone or dexamethasone as the glucocorticoid, so 'prednisolone' is a defensible but non-canonical substitute. Ref: Ross DS et al. ATA 2016 Hyperthyroidism Guidelines, Thyroid; Wiersinga WM et al. Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2023.

raw.Connection Title: Calcium-raising and phosphate-lowering actions of PTH
raw.Explanation: PTH conserves renal calcium, promotes phosphaturia, stimulates calcitriol formation and indirectly increases osteoclast-mediated resorption through osteoblast-lineage cells.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: PTH actions; Parathyroid hormone effects
raw.Source Section: Parathyroid Location and Function, p. 35
raw.Notes: Distal tubular Ca reabsorption, phosphaturia, renal 1-alpha-hydroxylase induction, and (indirect, RANKL-mediated via osteoblast-lineage cells) osteoclastic resorption are core PTH actions; resorption assumes sustained PTH signaling and is not direct on osteoclasts. Ref: Walker MD, Silverberg SJ. Nat Rev Endocrinol 2018; Guyton & Hall 14e.

raw.Notes: Celiac, cystic fibrosis, IBD, and gastric bypass impair absorption of fat-soluble vitamin D; malabsorption is not universal in all IBD or after every bypass, so 'predispose' wording is appropriate. Ref: Williams Textbook of Endocrinology 14e.

raw.Connection Title: Typical laboratory tendencies in primary hyperparathyroidism
raw.Explanation: Autonomous PTH secretion can raise calcium, promote phosphate loss and increase bone turnover with alkaline phosphatase elevation.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Primary hyperparathyroidism laboratory profile; PTH-driven hypercalcemia
raw.Source Section: Hyperparathyroidism: Primary, p. 38
raw.Notes: High Ca, high or inappropriately-normal PTH, and low phosphate are typical of primary HPT; ALP is often NORMAL in mild disease and PTH may be inappropriately normal rather than frankly elevated - this is a 'typical profile', not diagnostic criteria. Ref: Walker MD, Silverberg SJ. Nat Rev Endocrinol 2018; Bilezikian JP et al. Lancet 2018; Insogna KL. NEJM 2018.

raw.Connection Title: Laboratory pattern of CKD-related secondary hyperparathyroidism
raw.Explanation: Impaired renal phosphate excretion and calcitriol generation can lower calcium and stimulate secondary PTH secretion in CKD.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Renal secondary hyperparathyroidism; CKD mineral metabolism changes
raw.Source Section: Hyperparathyroidism: Secondary, p. 38
raw.Notes: Phosphate retention and reduced calcitriol drive low/low-normal Ca and elevated PTH in CKD; values vary with CKD stage and therapy, so the low-normal calcium qualifier avoids making hypocalcemia universal. Ref: KDIGO 2017 CKD-MBD Guideline; Williams Textbook of Endocrinology 14e.

raw.Connection Title: Laboratory clues to untreated primary adrenal insufficiency
raw.Explanation: Adrenal failure lowers cortisol and mineralocorticoid output. Loss of cortisol feedback raises ACTH; mineralocorticoid deficiency can impair potassium excretion.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Addison disease laboratory clues; Primary adrenal failure
raw.Source Section: Primary Adrenal Insufficiency: Diagnostics, p. 44
raw.Notes: High ACTH, low cortisol, low aldosterone, and hyperkalemia characterize untreated primary AI; hyperkalemia is present in only ~50% at diagnosis, and preserved aldosterone distinguishes secondary/tertiary AI. Ref: Vaidya A et al. Adrenal Insufficiency. JAMA 2025; Husebye ES et al. J Intern Med 2014; Bornstein SR et al. Endocrine Society 2016.

raw.Connection Title: Characteristic physical findings of Cushing syndrome
raw.Explanation: Excess glucocorticoid effect produces skin and connective-tissue changes and altered fat distribution, including these findings.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Cushingoid appearance; Physical findings of glucocorticoid excess
raw.Source Section: Hypercortisolism: Presentation, p. 47
raw.Notes: Purple striae, thin skin, central adiposity, and dorsocervical fat pad reflect glucocorticoid excess and also fit chronic exogenous steroid effect; do not label 'Cushing disease' (pituitary-source-specific). Ref: Nieman LK et al. Endocrine Society Cushing Guideline, JCEM 2008.

raw.Explanation: Reduced effective renal perfusion in heart or liver failure, renal artery narrowing and a renin-secreting tumor can activate renin-mediated aldosterone production.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: High-renin hyperaldosteronism; Secondary aldosterone excess

raw.Notes: CHF, cirrhosis/liver failure, renal artery stenosis, and reninoma cause renin-driven (secondary) hyperaldosteronism via reduced effective renal perfusion or autonomous renin secretion; liver-failure link depends on effective arterial underfilling. 'Increased renin' is an accepted mechanism-based alternate category. Ref: Williams Textbook of Endocrinology 14e.

raw.Connection Title: Molecular and diagnostic associations of neuroblastoma
raw.Explanation: Neuroblastoma can show MYCN amplification, increased catecholamine metabolites in urine and neuroblastic rosettes on microscopy.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Neuroblastoma clues; Neuroblastoma tumor associations
raw.Source Section: Adrenal Neoplasms: Neuroblastoma, p. 50
raw.Notes: MYCN amplification (prognostic subset, not universal), urinary VMA and HVA (distinct catecholamine metabolites), and Homer-Wright rosettes characterize neuroblastoma; rosettes also occur in other neural tumors. Ref: Nelson Textbook of Pediatrics 21e; Robbins & Cotran 10e.

raw.Connection Title: Recessive enzyme defects affecting sex-steroid synthesis or activation
raw.Explanation: The source groups these inherited enzyme defects when evaluating differences in sex development and describes each as autosomal recessive. They affect androgen synthesis or androgen activation.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Autosomal recessive steroid enzyme deficiencies; Recessive defects of androgen synthesis or activation
raw.Source Section: Adrenal Cortex Pathways Overview and Enzyme Deficiencies, pp. 51-56
raw.Notes: All four are autosomal recessive enzyme deficiencies of sex-steroid synthesis (21-OH, 17-alpha-OH, 11-beta-OH) or androgen activation (5-alpha-reductase). CRITICAL: 5-alpha-reductase deficiency is NOT a form of CAH - never accept an 'all are CAH' label. Shared autosomal recessive inheritance is the clean unifying category. Ref: El-Maouche D et al. CAH, Lancet 2017; Thigpen AE et al. NEJM 1992; MedlinePlus '5-alpha reductase deficiency'.

raw.Explanation: Impaired 17-alpha-hydroxylation reduces sex-steroid synthesis while increasing mineralocorticoid-active precursors, producing hypertension and potassium loss.

raw.Source Section: 17-alpha-hydroxylase Deficiency, p. 53
raw.Notes: 17-alpha-hydroxylase (CYP17A1) deficiency: elevated DOC/corticosterone -> hypertension + hypokalemia with REDUCED androgens/sex steroids; low androgens is the discriminator from 11-beta-OH deficiency. raw.Connection Title: Clues to 5-alpha-reductase deficiency in a 46,XY patient
raw.Explanation: Reduced conversion of testosterone to DHT impairs DHT-dependent external development while preserving testosterone-dependent internal structures. Pubertal testosterone increases can cause virilization.

Ref: Thigpen AE et al. NEJM 1992; Reyes AP et al. Nat Rev Urol 2023; MedlinePlus.

raw.Connection Title: Renal pathologic findings of diabetic nephropathy
raw.Explanation: Chronic diabetic injury can thicken the glomerular basement membrane, scar glomeruli and produce hyaline deposition in both afferent and efferent arterioles.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Diabetic nephropathy pathology; Diabetic renal microvascular injury
raw.Source Section: Diabetic Complications: Non-enzymatic Glycation, p. 64
raw.Notes: GBM thickening, (Kimmelstiel-Wilson nodular) glomerulosclerosis, and hyalinosis of BOTH afferent and efferent arterioles characterize diabetic nephropathy; efferent arteriolar involvement helps distinguish it from hypertensive nephrosclerosis (afferent-predominant). Not all lesions in every patient. Ref: Robbins & Cotran 10e.

raw.Connection Title: Sulfonylureas that stimulate insulin release via KATP-channel closure
raw.Explanation: These sulfonylureas close beta-cell ATP-sensitive potassium channels, causing depolarization and calcium-dependent insulin secretion.

raw.Connection Title: Source-listed glucose-lowering agents associated with weight loss
raw.Explanation: The source associates metformin, SGLT2 inhibition and the two named GLP1 agonists with weight loss. These effects differ in magnitude and are not guaranteed.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Diabetes medications associated with weight loss; Weight-reducing antihyperglycemic drugs
raw.Source Section: Diabetes Type 2: Management, p. 68
raw.Notes: Metformin (weight-neutral to modest ~2-3% loss), SGLT2 inhibitor (dapagliflozin), and GLP-1 agonists (exenatide, liraglutide) are associated with weight loss; magnitude GLP-1 > SGLT2 > metformin. 'Associated with', not guaranteed; metformin may be weight-neutral. Ref: Davies MJ et al. ADA/EASD 2022, Diabetologia; Tsapas A et al. Diabetes Obes Metab 2021 (network meta-analysis).

raw.Connection Title: Physiologic inhibitors of gastric acid secretion
raw.Explanation: Somatostatin is the principal physiologic inhibitor of gastric acid; secretin inhibits acid via somatostatin and prostaglandin release; cholecystokinin inhibits acid largely by stimulating somatostatin; prostaglandin E2 directly inhibits parietal cells (EP3/Gi). The original GIP tile was replaced because GIP inhibits acid only at supraphysiologic doses and is not a physiologic inhibitor in humans.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Enterogastrones; Physiologic inhibitors of gastric H+ secretion
raw.Source Section: Stomach / Gastric Regulation; Intestinal Regulation; Parietal Cell Physiology; PDF pp. 36, 38-39
raw.Notes: REVISED: GIP replaced by cholecystokinin. GIP acid inhibition is a pharmacologic artifact (name changed from gastric inhibitory to glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide). Added refs: Baggio & Drucker, Gastroenterology 2007; Nauck et al., Digestion 1992; Meier et al., World J Gastroenterol 2006; Schubert & Rehfeld, Compr Physiol 2019; Chung et al., Gastroenterology 1994. Board overlap: shares secretin and CCK with GI-012; do not use both on one board.

raw.Connection Title: Intestinal hormones that slow gastric emptying
raw.Explanation: Secretin, CCK, peptide YY, and GLP-1 are intestinal ('ileal brake') hormones that slow gastric emptying, coordinating delivery of chyme with intestinal digestive capacity. The original GIP tile was replaced because controlled human studies show GIP does not slow gastric emptying and may slightly accelerate it.

raw.Notes: Preserve can cause wording. Celiac-related B12 deficiency is legitimate but less characteristic than iron/folate (terminal ileum relatively spared). raw.Connection Title: Therapies that reduce copper burden in Wilson disease

raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Wilson disease copper-reducing measures
raw.Source Section: Liver / Wilson Disease; PDF pp. 65
raw.Notes: Different roles/mechanisms; category does not imply interchangeability or simultaneous use. Verified against AASLD Wilson Disease Practice Guidance 2022.

raw.Connection Title: Measures used to remove/reduce excess iron

raw.Source Section: Liver / Hereditary Hemochromatosis; PDF pp. 66
raw.Notes: Do not imply interchangeable first-line roles: phlebotomy is first-line for HFE hemochromatosis, chelators primarily for transfusional overload. Verified against Kane et al., Am Fam Physician 2021 and Powell et al., Lancet 2016.

raw.Connection Title: Markers of impaired synthetic/metabolic function in advanced cirrhosis

raw.Source Section: Liver / Cirrhosis; PDF pp. 68-69
raw.Notes: Qualifier: PT/INR reflects synthetic function, not net bleeding risk in cirrhosis (rebalanced hemostasis); not all abnormalities are present simultaneously. Verified against Robbins & Cotran, 10th ed.

raw.Notes: Do not claim a uniformly elevated HVPG: HVPG is normal in prehepatic and presinusoidal causes. Verified against Robbins & Cotran, 10th ed.

raw.Connection Title: Unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia from reduced UGT1A1 conjugation
raw.Explanation: Each features reduced bilirubin UDP-glucuronosyltransferase (UGT1A1) activity - mild in Gilbert, near-absent in Crigler-Najjar type I, partial in type II, and developmentally immature in physiologic neonatal jaundice - producing indirect hyperbilirubinemia.

raw.Notes: CN type I and II are distinct subtypes; physiologic neonatal jaundice also reflects increased RBC turnover and enterohepatic recycling. Board overlap: shares physiologic neonatal jaundice with GI-032. Verified against Robbins & Cotran, 10th ed.

raw.Connection Title: Imaging and examination clues to acute cholecystitis
raw.Explanation: Cystic-duct obstruction and inflammation produce a positive Murphy sign, sonographic gallbladder wall thickening (>3 mm) and pericholecystic fluid, and nonvisualization of the gallbladder on HIDA (cholescintigraphy).
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Acute cholecystitis diagnostic findings
raw.Source Section: Biliary System / Acute Cholecystitis; PDF pp. 96
raw.Notes: Individual ultrasound signs are nonspecific; HIDA nonvisualization is sensitive but requires correct timing and has false positives. Verified against Robbins & Cotran, 10th ed.

raw.Connection Title: Causes of acute pancreatitis beyond alcohol and gallstones
raw.Explanation: These metabolic (triglycerides >=1000 mg/dL; hypercalcemia), infectious (mumps), and iatrogenic (post-ERCP) factors are recognized triggers of acute pancreatitis.

raw.Connection Title: Diagnostic pattern of chronic pancreatic exocrine insufficiency
raw.Explanation: Advanced chronic pancreatitis shows ductal calcifications and parenchymal atrophy with low fecal elastase (exocrine insufficiency), while normal D-xylose testing indicates intact small-bowel mucosal absorption - distinguishing pancreatic from mucosal malabsorption.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Chronic pancreatitis diagnostic pattern
raw.Source Section: Pancreas / Chronic Pancreatitis; PDF pp. 127
raw.Notes: Normal D-xylose assumes no coexisting mucosal disease; calcifications and low elastase are not universal. Verified against Robbins & Cotran, 10th ed. and Yamada's Textbook of Gastroenterology, 7th ed.

raw.Explanation: Excess somatostatin inhibits insulin (diabetes/hyperglycemia), gallbladder contraction and CCK (cholelithiasis), and pancreatic exocrine secretion (steatorrhea), with accompanying weight loss.

Normal ammonia is a lab discriminator, not a symptom.

raw.Connection Title: Vaso-occlusive complications of sickle cell disease
raw.Explanation: Vaso-occlusion drives dactylitis, acute chest syndrome, avascular necrosis (osteonecrosis), and ischemic stroke in sickle cell disease. Acute chest syndrome is multifactorial (infection, fat embolism, infarction), so this is an association with vaso-occlusion rather than an exclusive cause.

raw.Source Section: PDF p. 41 | Key Mutations > Sickle Cell Anemia
raw.Notes: Verified (Ware et al., Lancet 2017; Piel et al., NEJM 2017). Acute chest syndrome and stroke are not single-mechanism; keep association wording.

raw.Connection Title: Williams syndrome cardiovascular and metabolic associations
raw.Explanation: Williams syndrome (7q11.23 deletion including ELN) causes an elastin arteriopathy with supravalvular aortic stenosis and other arterial stenoses (e.g., renal artery), plus idiopathic hypercalcemia (~15-45%). The ELN deletion underlies the vascular phenotype; the other tiles are clinical associations.

raw.Notes: Verified (Morris & Braddock, AAP Williams syndrome guideline 2020; Kozel et al., Nat Rev Dis Primers 2021; MedlinePlus). ELN deletion explains the arteriopathy (SVAS, renal/other arterial stenoses); hypercalcemia mechanism is distinct and not universal. Mixing a genetic lesion with clinical findings is intentional and medically coherent.
